bull.t: Strong cash generation and free cash flow
bull.b: Gilead’s persistent ability to convert earnings into cash and a material recent jump in free cash flow underpins durable financial flexibility. Strong cash generation supports sustained R&D funding, commercialization of launches, dividends or buybacks, and integration of acquisitions over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Robust HIV franchise and raised HIV guidance
bull.b: The HIV franchise remains a structural growth engine with double-digit sales gains and an uplifted guidance range. Persistent demand for core regimens and expanding PrEP adoption create predictable revenue flows, supporting long-term margin durability and providing a platform to fund pipeline and new launches over 2–6 months and beyond.

Trodelvy’s accelerating sales and label expansions diversify Gilead’s revenue base and increase addressable market. Sustained oncology approvals and strong commercial traction create durable higher-margin revenue streams and strengthen the company’s strategic shift into oncology over the medium term.

bear.t: Massive acquired IPR&D charges distort GAAP results
bear.b: Very large acquisition-related IPR&D charges materially depress GAAP profitability and reported EPS, obscuring operational performance. These non-deductible and non-recurring accounting charges complicate comparability, tax outcomes, and stakeholder assessment of sustainable earnings and could weigh on credit metrics and guidance interpretation.

bear.t: TTM swing to reported losses and balance-sheet reporting ambiguity
bear.b: Trailing twelve‑month reported losses signal volatility in profitability despite prior strength, while an abrupt TTM debt reporting change (debt shown at zero) undermines confidence in leverage trends. This ambiguity makes it harder to assess structural solvency and financing capacity over the medium term.

bear.t: Cell therapy revenue weakness and competitive pressure
bear.b: Declining cell therapy sales reflect in‑class competition and demand pressure, weakening a key diversification pillar. Sustained declines could reduce expected upside from recent cell therapy acquisitions, constrain margin improvement, and require incremental investment to defend market share over the next several quarters.
